title: The Internet
short: A global network of networks that exchange data using shared protocols.
description: The Internet is a global network of interconnected networks that communicate using the Internet Protocol suite. Its architecture allows independently operated networks to exchange data, with information commonly divided into packets and routed across multiple links. The Internet emerged from research into packet switching and internetworking, with ARPANET among its important predecessors and TCP/IP becoming central to its expansion. It is distinct from the World Wide Web: the Web is one information system that runs on top of the Internet.

title: World Wide Web
short: A global information system built on the Internet, linking documents and resources through URLs and hyperlinks.
description: The World Wide Web is an information system that runs on the Internet. It connects resources through URLs and hyperlinks and uses web standards and protocols such as HTTP and HTML so browsers and servers can exchange and display information. Tim Berners-Lee proposed the system at CERN in 1989; the first browser and server were developed in 1990, and the Web was made freely usable in 1993. The Web is not the Internet itself: it is one service built on top of the Internet.

title: Modern Computer
short: A programmable machine that represents, stores and processes information according to instructions.
description: A computer is a programmable machine that accepts data, processes it according to instructions, stores information and produces results. Modern electronic digital computers grew from several lines of mathematical, theoretical and engineering work rather than one single invention. A defining development was the stored-program architecture, in which instructions and data are held in memory. Early electronic computers differed in purpose, technology and design, so claims about the 'first computer' depend on the criteria being used.

title: Alan Turing
short: A pioneer of theoretical computer science.
description: Alan Turing formalized the idea of a general-purpose computing machine and made foundational contributions to codebreaking and artificial intelligence.

title: Artificial Intelligence
short: A broad field developing computational systems that perform tasks associated with intelligent behaviour.
description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is a broad field concerned with building computational systems that perform tasks commonly associated with human intelligence, such as perception, language processing, learning, reasoning and decision-making. Approaches include symbolic methods, statistical machine learning and deep neural networks. Capabilities vary widely by task, and fluent output should not be confused with human understanding or general intelligence. Responsible development also involves evaluating reliability, bias, security, privacy and the effects of deploying AI in real settings.

title: Printing Press
short: Printing technologies reproduce text and images at scale, transforming how knowledge is copied and circulated.
description: Printing is the reproduction of text or images from prepared forms onto materials such as paper. Printing developed in East Asia long before Gutenberg, including woodblock printing and movable type. In mid-fifteenth-century Europe, Johannes Gutenberg and his workshop refined a system using reusable metal type, suitable inks and a mechanical press. This made repeated production of books more practical and helped accelerate the circulation of texts, while remaining part of a much longer global history of printing.

title: Electricity
short: A set of physical phenomena associated with electric charge, including its forces, fields and movement.
description: Electricity describes physical phenomena associated with electric charge, including static charge, electric fields, voltage and electric current. It is not itself a primary energy source: generators convert other forms of energy into electrical energy, often through electromagnetic induction. The study of electricity developed through contributions from many investigators, and practical electrical systems later transformed lighting, industry, communication and everyday life.

title: Isaac Newton
short: Laws of motion and universal gravitation.
description: Newton's laws of motion and universal gravitation unified the study of motion on Earth and in the heavens, shaping classical physics.

title: Albert Einstein
short: Reimagined space, time and gravity.
description: Einstein's theories of special and general relativity transformed physics and changed how scientists understand space, time, energy and gravity.

title: Evolution
short: How inherited variation changes populations over generations and produces life's diversity.
description: Biological evolution is change in the heritable characteristics of populations across generations. Mutation introduces genetic variation, while natural selection, genetic drift and gene flow alter how variants are distributed. Evolution explains both adaptation and the shared ancestry of living organisms, supported by evidence from fossils, genetics, comparative anatomy and biogeography. Individuals do not evolve during their lifetimes; populations evolve as inherited variants become more or less common over generations.

title: DNA Structure
short: A double-stranded molecular structure that stores hereditary information in living systems.
description: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) is a molecule that stores hereditary information in nearly all cellular organisms. It consists of nucleotide units arranged in two antiparallel strands that form a double helix. The bases pair specifically: adenine with thymine, and guanine with cytosine. This complementary structure allows DNA to be copied, while sequences of DNA contribute to the production and regulation of RNA and proteins. Not all DNA directly encodes proteins; substantial regions have regulatory and other functions.

title: Moon Landing
short: Humanity's first steps on another world.
description: Apollo 11 landed astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the Moon in July 1969, a defining moment in space exploration.

title: Apollo Program
short: A bold engineering journey to the Moon.
description: NASA's Apollo program mobilized scientific, industrial and engineering expertise to land humans on the Moon and return them safely.

title: Renaissance
short: Art, inquiry and ideas flourished.
description: The Renaissance was a period of renewed interest in classical learning, artistic experimentation and human-centered inquiry across Europe.

title: Industrial Revolution
short: The long, uneven transformation from predominantly agrarian production toward mechanized industry, factory work and fossil-fuel-powered economies.
description: The Industrial Revolution describes the transition toward mechanized production, factory systems and new energy and transport networks, beginning in Britain in the eighteenth century before spreading unevenly across the world. It transformed work, urban life, trade and economic organization, while also intensifying pollution, harsh labour conditions, colonial extraction and social disruption. It was not a single event or a uniform process; different regions industrialized at different times and through distinct paths.

title: Steam Engine
short: A heat engine that uses steam pressure and expansion to produce mechanical work.
description: A steam engine is a heat engine that uses steam to produce mechanical work. Early practical atmospheric engines, including Thomas Newcomen's engine installed in 1712, were used mainly to pump water from mines. James Watt and many other engineers later improved efficiency, control and applications. Steam power became central to industrialisation, transport and manufacturing, but its history was cumulative rather than the work of one inventor.

title: World War II
short: A conflict that reshaped the modern world.
description: World War II was a global conflict that transformed geopolitics, technology, international institutions and societies.

title: Transistor
short: A semiconductor device used to amplify or switch electronic signals and electrical power.
description: A transistor is a semiconductor device that can control current or voltage, allowing it to act as an electronic switch or amplifier. John Bardeen and Walter Brattain demonstrated a working point-contact transistor at Bell Labs in December 1947; William Shockley subsequently developed the junction-transistor theory and device. Different transistor types and manufacturing advances made electronics smaller, more reliable and more energy-efficient, enabling modern digital computers and communications.

title: Semiconductors
short: A material whose electrical conductivity can be deliberately controlled, forming the basis of modern electronic devices.
description: A semiconductor is a material whose electrical conductivity lies between that of a good conductor and an insulator and can be controlled by factors such as doping, temperature, light and electric fields. Silicon is the most widely used semiconductor in modern electronics. Semiconductor physics and manufacturing make devices such as diodes, transistors, sensors and integrated circuits possible. The field developed through contributions from physics, chemistry, materials science and industrial engineering.

title: Smartphone
short: A computer and camera in your pocket.
description: The modern smartphone combines mobile communication, computing, cameras, sensors and Internet access in a pocket-sized device.

title: Climate Change
short: Long-term shifts in climate, with current global warming driven mainly by human greenhouse-gas emissions.
description: Climate change refers to long-term shifts in temperatures and weather patterns. Earth's climate has changed naturally in the past, but the rapid warming observed since the mid-twentieth century is primarily caused by human activities, especially greenhouse-gas emissions from burning fossil fuels, land-use change and industry. Evidence includes rising global temperatures, warming oceans, shrinking glaciers and ice sheets, and rising sea levels. Understanding climate change requires both physical climate science and study of impacts, adaptation and emissions reduction.

title: Charles Darwin
short: Natural selection changed biology.
description: Charles Darwin developed the theory of evolution by natural selection, providing a unifying explanation for the diversity of life.

title: Vaccination
short: A way to train immune defenses to recognize specific pathogens before exposure.
description: Vaccination is the process of exposing the immune system to an antigen or antigen instructions so it can develop protection against a particular infectious disease. Depending on the vaccine platform, this may involve weakened or inactivated pathogens, selected components, or genetic instructions that let cells produce an antigen. Immune responses can include antibodies and immune memory, reducing the risk of severe disease. Protection is not always complete, and its strength and duration vary by vaccine, pathogen and person.

title: Johannes Gutenberg
short: A key figure in European printing history.
description: Gutenberg developed a practical movable-type printing system in Europe, helping make books more widely available.

title: Miguel de Cervantes
short: Author of Don Quixote.
description: Cervantes wrote Don Quixote, a landmark work often considered one of the foundations of the modern novel.

title: TCP/IP
short: The Internet protocol suite enables independent networks and devices to exchange data using common rules.
description: The Internet protocol suite, commonly called TCP/IP, is a layered set of rules that allows different computers and networks to communicate. Internet Protocol (IP) addresses and forwards packets across interconnected networks, while Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) provides a reliable, ordered byte stream between applications. Other transport protocols, including UDP, serve different needs. TCP/IP is not one program or a single protocol; it is an evolving family of interoperable standards.

title: Artificial Satellites
short: A human-made object placed in orbit to support communication, navigation, observation and scientific research.
description: An artificial satellite is a human-made object placed into orbit around Earth or another celestial body. Satellites can relay communications, support navigation and timing, observe weather and environmental change, map Earth, and conduct scientific experiments. The Soviet Union's Sputnik 1, launched on 4 October 1957, was the first artificial satellite to orbit Earth and marked the beginning of the Space Age.

title: GPS
short: A satellite-based radionavigation system that lets receivers calculate position, velocity and precise time.
description: The Global Positioning System (GPS) is a satellite-based radionavigation system that provides positioning, navigation and timing services worldwide. GPS satellites broadcast precisely timed signals and information about their orbits; a receiver compares signal arrival times from multiple satellites to estimate its position and clock offset. The system has space, control and user segments. GPS began as a United States defence programme, with its first NAVSTAR satellite launched in 1978, and later became a widely used civilian infrastructure.

title: Reformation
short: A movement transformed by printed ideas.
description: The Protestant Reformation reshaped European religious and political life. The printing press helped pamphlets and translations circulate widely.

title: Globalization
short: People, economies and cultures interconnect.
description: Globalization describes the growing connections among countries through trade, technology, migration, culture and communication.

title: Agricultural Revolution
description: The Neolithic transition to agriculture occurred independently in several regions rather than beginning at one universal point. Communities domesticated different crops and animals in Southwest Asia, East Asia, New Guinea, Africa and the Americas at different times. Farming supported more permanent settlements and, in many places, population growth and new forms of social organization, but it also brought new disease patterns, inequalities and environmental change. The transition was gradual and did not replace hunting and gathering everywhere.
short: The gradual adoption of plant cultivation and animal domestication by human communities in multiple regions of the world.

title: Writing
description: Writing preserved laws, records, stories and knowledge beyond spoken memory.
short: Writing preserved laws, records, stories and knowledge beyond spoken memory.

title: Mesopotamia
description: Mesopotamia refers to the historical region associated with the Tigris and Euphrates river systems, largely in modern Iraq and extending into neighbouring countries. From the late fourth millennium BCE, communities in southern Mesopotamia developed some of the earliest known cities and writing systems, including cuneiform. Sumerian, Akkadian, Babylonian and Assyrian societies changed over millennia, building complex institutions, trade networks, irrigation works and scholarly traditions. Mesopotamia was diverse and interacted continuously with surrounding regions.
short: A historical region between and around the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, home to several early urban civilizations.

title: Ancient Greece
description: The Greek world shaped later traditions in philosophy, mathematics, political thought, drama and scientific inquiry.
short: The Greek world shaped later traditions in philosophy, mathematics, political thought, drama and scientific inquiry.

title: Democracy
description: Democracy grounds political authority in the people and has roots in several ancient societies and many modern forms.
short: Democracy grounds political authority in the people and has roots in several ancient societies and many modern forms.

title: Roman Empire
description: The Roman state developed from a city in central Italy into a republic and then a Mediterranean empire. The imperial period conventionally begins in 27 BCE, when Octavian received the title Augustus. Roman rule connected diverse provinces through administration, roads, ports, military systems, law, trade and cultural exchange, while relying heavily on conquest, taxation, slavery and unequal power. The western imperial government ended in the fifth century CE, while the eastern Roman, or Byzantine, Empire continued for centuries.
short: An ancient Mediterranean state whose republican and imperial institutions shaped large parts of Europe, North Africa and western Asia.

title: Silk Road
description: The Silk Roads were not one road but changing networks of overland and maritime routes linking East Asia, Central Asia, South Asia, the Middle East, Africa and Europe. They carried goods such as silk, spices, ceramics and metals, as well as technologies, religious traditions, languages, artistic forms and scientific knowledge. These exchanges were shaped by geography, political power, commercial demand and changing security conditions. The networks expanded and shifted across many centuries.
short: A changing network of Eurasian and maritime trade routes that connected societies through commerce, migration and cultural exchange.

title: Paper
description: Paper is a sheet material made by forming a mat of separated fibres, usually plant-based, and drying it into a flexible surface. Paper-making developed in China in the early centuries CE; historical evidence for early paper predates the later account of Cai Lun, who is traditionally associated with improvements to its production around 105 CE. The technique spread across Asia and later westward through interconnected trade and knowledge networks, reshaping administration, scholarship and publishing.
short: A thin, flexible sheet material that transformed record-keeping, education, administration and publishing.

title: Magnetic Compass
description: A magnetic compass uses a magnetised needle or other element that aligns approximately with Earth's magnetic field, helping users determine direction. Knowledge of magnetism and magnetic direction in China predates the first surviving written descriptions of compass use for navigation. By the medieval period, compasses had become important tools for overland and maritime travel. A compass points toward magnetic north, which differs from true geographic north and varies by location and time.
short: A navigation instrument that uses a magnetised element to indicate direction relative to Earth's magnetic field.

title: Gunpowder
description: Developed in China, gunpowder changed warfare and later influenced mining, engineering and artillery.
short: Developed in China, gunpowder changed warfare and later influenced mining, engineering and artillery.

title: Nicolaus Copernicus
description: Copernicus proposed a heliocentric model in which Earth and the other planets orbit the Sun.
short: Copernicus proposed a heliocentric model in which Earth and the other planets orbit the Sun.

title: Galileo Galilei
description: Galileo used telescopic observations and experiments to reshape astronomy and the study of motion.
short: Galileo used telescopic observations and experiments to reshape astronomy and the study of motion.

title: Telescope
description: The telescope made distant celestial objects observable in greater detail and transformed astronomy.
short: The telescope made distant celestial objects observable in greater detail and transformed astronomy.

title: Microscope
description: The microscope revealed structures too small to see unaided, opening new paths in biology and medicine.
short: The microscope revealed structures too small to see unaided, opening new paths in biology and medicine.

title: Scientific Method
description: The scientific method is not a single rigid checklist used identically in every discipline. It describes a family of practices through which researchers make observations, ask questions, develop testable explanations, gather evidence, analyse results and revise ideas. Experiments, measurement, replication, peer criticism and transparent reporting help make findings more dependable. Scientific explanations remain open to revision when new evidence or better methods become available.
short: A family of evidence-based practices for asking questions, testing explanations and revising knowledge.

title: Michael Faraday
description: Faraday's experiments on electromagnetic induction established principles behind electric generators and transformers.
short: Faraday's experiments on electromagnetic induction established principles behind electric generators and transformers.

title: James Clerk Maxwell
description: Maxwell unified electricity, magnetism and light in equations central to modern physics and communications.
short: Maxwell unified electricity, magnetism and light in equations central to modern physics and communications.

title: Telephone
description: The telephone transmits speech over electrical networks, reshaping personal and business communication.
short: The telephone transmits speech over electrical networks, reshaping personal and business communication.

title: Radio
description: Radio transmits information wirelessly and became central to broadcasting, navigation and communication.
short: Radio transmits information wirelessly and became central to broadcasting, navigation and communication.

title: Airplane
description: Powered flight transformed travel, trade, warfare and how people understand distance.
short: Powered flight transformed travel, trade, warfare and how people understand distance.

title: Germ Theory
description: Germ theory explains that many infectious diseases are caused by microorganisms such as bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites. It emerged through a long history of microscopy, experiments, clinical observation and public-health practice, with major nineteenth-century contributions from Louis Pasteur and Robert Koch. Germ theory transformed infection prevention, sanitation, food safety, vaccination and surgery. It does not mean every disease is infectious or has a microbial cause.
short: The scientific framework that explains many infectious diseases through disease-causing microorganisms.

title: Penicillin
description: Penicillin is a group of beta-lactam antibiotics that kill susceptible bacteria by interfering with cell-wall synthesis. Alexander Fleming observed the antibacterial effect of a Penicillium mould in 1928 and published his findings in 1929. A team at Oxford, including Howard Florey, Ernst Chain and Norman Heatley, later developed methods to purify, test and produce penicillin for clinical use during the 1940s. Its success transformed treatment of bacterial infections, while the spread of antibiotic resistance makes careful use essential.
short: An antibiotic first observed by Alexander Fleming and later developed into a widely usable medicine by a research team.

title: Smallpox
description: Smallpox was a severe infectious disease caused by variola viruses and spread mainly through close contact and respiratory exposure. It caused major mortality and lasting disability across many societies. The global eradication campaign combined vaccination, surveillance and containment; the last known naturally occurring case was recorded in 1977, and the World Health Assembly declared smallpox eradicated in 1980. It remains the only human infectious disease eradicated worldwide through deliberate public-health action.
short: A devastating infectious disease caused by variola virus that was declared eradicated in 1980.

title: Black Death
description: The Black Death devastated populations across Europe, Asia and North Africa and reshaped economies and social life.
short: The Black Death devastated populations across Europe, Asia and North Africa and reshaped economies and social life.

title: Leonardo da Vinci
description: Leonardo combined art, engineering and observation, exemplifying the broad curiosity associated with the Renaissance.
short: Leonardo combined art, engineering and observation, exemplifying the broad curiosity associated with the Renaissance.

title: Algebra
description: Algebra is a branch of mathematics that uses symbols to represent numbers and unknown quantities and studies the rules governing their relationships. Equation-solving traditions existed in ancient Babylonian, Greek and Indian mathematics. In the ninth century, the scholar Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi wrote an influential systematic treatise on al-jabr and al-muqabala, helping establish algebra as a distinct discipline and giving the subject its name. Modern symbolic notation developed gradually over later centuries.
short: A branch of mathematics that studies relationships and structures using symbols, quantities and rules.

title: Zero
description: Zero has two closely related but distinct roles: it is a number representing no quantity, and it marks an empty place in a positional numeral system. Different societies developed forms of zero independently or through distinct historical pathways. Indian mathematicians developed the decimal place-value system and treated zero as a number; Brahmagupta set out arithmetic rules involving zero in the seventh century. The history is cumulative and should not be reduced to a single inventor or date.
short: A number representing no quantity and a placeholder that makes positional numeral systems work.

title: Indus Valley Civilisation
description: The Indus Valley Civilisation built planned cities with drainage, standardized weights and extensive South Asian trade.
short: The Indus Valley Civilisation built planned cities with drainage, standardized weights and extensive South Asian trade.

title: Buddhism
description: Buddhism emerged in ancient India and spread across Asia through teaching, travel, translation and trade networks.
short: Buddhism emerged in ancient India and spread across Asia through teaching, travel, translation and trade networks.

title: Big Bang
description: The leading scientific model describes the universe expanding from an extremely hot, dense early state. It is supported by observations including cosmic expansion and the cosmic microwave background.
short: The leading scientific model describes the universe expanding from an extremely hot, dense early state. It is supported by observations including cosmic expansion and the cosmic microwave background.

title: Edwin Hubble
description: Hubble's observations of distant galaxies showed that the universe is expanding, transforming modern cosmology.
short: Hubble's observations of distant galaxies showed that the universe is expanding, transforming modern cosmology.

title: Quantum Mechanics
description: Quantum mechanics is the framework physicists use to describe matter and energy at atomic and subatomic scales. A system is represented by a quantum state, often expressed as a wave function, from which probabilities for measurement outcomes can be calculated. Superposition, quantized observables and the uncertainty principle distinguish quantum theory from classical descriptions. The framework underlies technologies such as semiconductors, lasers and many forms of modern imaging, while its interpretation remains an active philosophical and scientific discussion.
short: The physical framework for matter and energy at atomic and subatomic scales.

title: Marie Curie
description: Marie Curie's research on radioactivity led to the discovery of polonium and radium and changed the study of atomic physics and medicine.
short: Marie Curie's research on radioactivity led to the discovery of polonium and radium and changed the study of atomic physics and medicine.

title: Radioactivity
description: Radioactivity is the spontaneous emission of radiation from unstable atomic nuclei, a phenomenon central to nuclear science and medical imaging.
short: Radioactivity is the spontaneous emission of radiation from unstable atomic nuclei, a phenomenon central to nuclear science and medical imaging.

title: X-rays
description: X-rays are high-energy electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths shorter than ultraviolet light. Their ability to pass through many materials, with different absorption by different tissues, makes them useful in medical imaging and industrial inspection. Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen identified the rays in 1895 while investigating electrical discharges in vacuum tubes; the discovery quickly transformed physics and medicine. X-rays are ionizing radiation, so medical use balances diagnostic benefit against exposure risk.
short: A form of electromagnetic radiation used in imaging because it can pass through materials and is absorbed differently by different substances.

title: Insulin
description: Insulin is a peptide hormone produced by pancreatic beta cells that helps regulate blood glucose by influencing glucose uptake, storage and metabolism. Research at the University of Toronto in 1921–1922, involving Frederick Banting, Charles Best, John Macleod and James Collip, led to the purification and clinical use of insulin. The discovery transformed diabetes care, but modern insulin treatment has continued to evolve through advances in manufacturing, formulations, delivery and monitoring.
short: A pancreatic hormone that helps regulate blood glucose and a life-saving therapy for people who cannot produce or use enough insulin.

title: Human Genome Project
description: The Human Genome Project was an international research programme, formally launched in 1990 and completed in 2003, to map and sequence human DNA and selected model organisms. Its 2003 reference sequence covered about 92% of the human genome with high accuracy by the technologies then available; it was not the complete genome of one individual. The project advanced sequencing technology, open data sharing and biomedical research. In 2022, the Telomere-to-Telomere consortium reported the first truly complete human genome sequence, filling major repetitive gaps left by earlier methods.
short: An international project that produced a reference sequence of human DNA and transformed modern genomics.

title: CRISPR
description: CRISPR-based tools made targeted genome editing more accessible and opened new possibilities and ethical questions in biology and medicine.
short: CRISPR-based tools made targeted genome editing more accessible and opened new possibilities and ethical questions in biology and medicine.

title: French Revolution
description: The French Revolution challenged monarchy and privilege, reshaped political institutions and helped spread ideas of citizenship and popular sovereignty.
short: The French Revolution challenged monarchy and privilege, reshaped political institutions and helped spread ideas of citizenship and popular sovereignty.

title: American Revolution
description: The thirteen colonies' break from British rule produced the United States and influenced later debates about republican government and rights.
short: The thirteen colonies' break from British rule produced the United States and influenced later debates about republican government and rights.

title: Gutenberg Bible
description: Among the earliest major books printed in Europe with movable metal type, the Gutenberg Bible demonstrates the scale and craft of early printing.
short: Among the earliest major books printed in Europe with movable metal type, the Gutenberg Bible demonstrates the scale and craft of early printing.

title: Mughal Empire
description: The Mughal Empire governed much of the Indian subcontinent and shaped its architecture, administration, languages, art and foodways.
short: The Mughal Empire governed much of the Indian subcontinent and shaped its architecture, administration, languages, art and foodways.

title: Bengal Renaissance
description: A period of social, literary, educational and scientific reform in Bengal, involving figures who debated modernity, identity and social change.
short: A period of social, literary, educational and scientific reform in Bengal, involving figures who debated modernity, identity and social change.

title: Bengali Language Movement
description: The movement in East Bengal demanded recognition of Bengali as a state language of Pakistan; its legacy is commemorated on International Mother Language Day.
short: The movement in East Bengal demanded recognition of Bengali as a state language of Pakistan; its legacy is commemorated on International Mother Language Day.

title: Bangladesh Liberation War
description: The 1971 war led to the independence of Bangladesh after a struggle involving mass displacement, atrocities and a decisive military campaign.
short: The 1971 war led to the independence of Bangladesh after a struggle involving mass displacement, atrocities and a decisive military campaign.

title: Dhaka
description: Dhaka grew as an important Mughal provincial capital and later became the capital of Bangladesh, shaped by rivers, trade and migration.
short: Dhaka grew as an important Mughal provincial capital and later became the capital of Bangladesh, shaped by rivers, trade and migration.

title: The Sundarbans
description: The Sundarbans is a transboundary mangrove ecosystem in the Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna delta shared by Bangladesh and India. Its tidal channels, mudflats and salt-tolerant forests support diverse terrestrial and aquatic life, including the Bengal tiger. The mangroves help stabilize shorelines, buffer storm impacts and support local livelihoods, while facing pressures from cyclones, salinity change, erosion, pollution and human land use. The Bangladesh and Indian portions have separate UNESCO World Heritage designations.
short: A large tidal mangrove ecosystem in the Bengal delta, shared by Bangladesh and India.

title: Rabindranath Tagore
description: Tagore reshaped Bengali literature and music and became the first non-European Nobel laureate in Literature in 1913.
short: Tagore reshaped Bengali literature and music and became the first non-European Nobel laureate in Literature in 1913.

title: Jagadish Chandra Bose
description: Bose pioneered research in radio and microwave optics and later investigated plant physiology, working across disciplinary boundaries.
short: Bose pioneered research in radio and microwave optics and later investigated plant physiology, working across disciplinary boundaries.

title: Pala Empire
description: The Pala dynasty ruled large parts of Bengal and Bihar and supported Buddhist institutions, scholarship and art across Asia.
short: The Pala dynasty ruled large parts of Bengal and Bihar and supported Buddhist institutions, scholarship and art across Asia.

title: Monsoon
description: Seasonal wind reversals bring concentrated rainfall across South and Southeast Asia, shaping agriculture, settlement and everyday life.
short: Seasonal wind reversals bring concentrated rainfall across South and Southeast Asia, shaping agriculture, settlement and everyday life.

title: Movable Type
description: Movable type was developed in China centuries before Gutenberg's European press, with technologies and materials evolving across regions.
short: Movable type was developed in China centuries before Gutenberg's European press, with technologies and materials evolving across regions.

title: Railway
description: Railways connected cities and markets at unprecedented speed and became central to industrialization, migration and empire.
short: Railways connected cities and markets at unprecedented speed and became central to industrialization, migration and empire.

title: Mobile Phone
description: Mobile telephony evolved from early cellular prototypes into global networks that reshaped personal communication and access to information.
short: Mobile telephony evolved from early cellular prototypes into global networks that reshaped personal communication and access to information.

title: Photography
description: Photography changed how people record events, represent identity and communicate evidence, art and memory.
short: Photography changed how people record events, represent identity and communicate evidence, art and memory.

title: Open Source Software
description: Open-source software makes source code available for inspection, modification and redistribution, supporting collaborative development across the world.
short: Open-source software makes source code available for inspection, modification and redistribution, supporting collaborative development across the world.

title: Renewable Energy
description: Renewable energy comes from sources replenished by natural processes on human timescales, including sunlight, wind, flowing water, geothermal heat and biomass. These resources can produce electricity, heat and fuels, but each technology has different costs, land and material needs, reliability characteristics and environmental effects. Renewable energy is therefore not impact-free; its role in energy systems depends on storage, transmission, demand management, local ecosystems and careful planning.
short: Energy from naturally replenished flows and processes, including sunlight, wind, water, geothermal heat and biomass.

title: Edward Jenner
description: Jenner's work using cowpox to protect against smallpox helped establish vaccination and eventually contributed to the eradication of the disease.
short: Jenner's work using cowpox to protect against smallpox helped establish vaccination and eventually contributed to the eradication of the disease.

title: Satyendra Nath Bose
short: A physicist whose work helped shape quantum statistics.
description: Satyendra Nath Bose was a Bengali physicist whose 1924 work on quantum statistics helped establish the foundation of Bose-Einstein statistics. The class of particles that follows this statistical description is named bosons in his honour.

title: Begum Rokeya
short: A Bengali writer and advocate of women's education.
description: Begum Rokeya Sakhawat Hossain was a Bengali writer, educator and social reformer. Her 1905 satire Sultana's Dream imagined a society led by women, while her work and educational initiatives challenged restrictions on women's learning and public life.

title: Battle of Plassey
short: A turning point in the East India Company's rise in Bengal.
description: Fought on 23 June 1757, the Battle of Plassey pitted the forces of Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah against the British East India Company led by Robert Clive. The Nawab's defeat, amid defections among his commanders, opened the way for the Company to expand its political and revenue power in Bengal.

title: Permanent Settlement
short: A colonial land system that reshaped rural Bengal.
description: Introduced by the East India Company in 1793 under Governor-General Lord Cornwallis, the Permanent Settlement fixed the land revenue owed by zamindars to the colonial state and recognised them as proprietors. Cultivators did not receive equivalent protections, and the system reshaped agrarian power and rent relations in Bengal.

title: Partition of Bengal
short: A controversial division that transformed politics in Bengal.
description: The British government partitioned Bengal on 16 October 1905, creating the province of Eastern Bengal and Assam alongside a reorganised western province. Officials presented the change as administrative reorganisation, while opposition to it fuelled the Swadeshi movement. The partition was annulled in 1911.

title: Swadeshi Movement
short: A campaign for locally made goods and resistance to partition.
description: The Swadeshi movement grew in response to the 1905 Partition of Bengal. Supporters promoted locally made goods, boycotted many British imports and built campaigns around education, public meetings and indigenous enterprise. Its social and political character varied across communities and regions.

title: Somapura Mahavihara
short: A major Buddhist learning centre at Paharpur, Bangladesh.
description: Built under the Pala ruler Dharmapala, Somapura Mahavihara at Paharpur became a renowned Buddhist intellectual centre. Its monumental central shrine, quadrangular monastery and terracotta decoration influenced Buddhist architecture beyond Bengal. UNESCO inscribed the ruins as a World Heritage Site in 1985.

title: University of Dhaka
short: An institution central to education and public life in Bangladesh.
description: The University of Dhaka began teaching on 1 July 1921 with faculties of Arts, Science and Law. Its students, teachers and alumni later played important roles in the intellectual, cultural and political life of the region, including movements that shaped Bangladesh.

title: Six-Point Movement
short: A programme demanding far-reaching autonomy for East Pakistan.
description: Presented by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in 1966, the Six-Point Programme called for a federal structure with limited central powers and substantial autonomy for East Pakistan, including control over taxation and economic policy. It became a major organising platform in the political struggle that preceded Bangladesh's independence.

title: Mass Uprising of 1969
short: A mass movement that challenged military rule in East Pakistan.
description: The 1969 mass uprising brought students, workers and wider sections of society into protests against the Ayub Khan regime in Pakistan. The movement helped force the withdrawal of the Agartala Conspiracy Case and the release of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, weakening the regime's authority in East Pakistan.

title: Bengal Famine of 1943
short: A devastating famine in wartime Bengal.
description: The Bengal famine of 1943 caused mass starvation and disease across the region during the Second World War. Historians examine interacting causes including wartime disruption, inflation, food-market failures, policy decisions and unequal access to food. Estimates of deaths vary by source and method.

title: The Bengal Delta
short: A river-shaped region with a long, connected history.
description: The Bengal delta is formed by the Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna river systems. Its waterways, fertile floodplains and links to the Bay of Bengal shaped settlement, agriculture, trade and cultural exchange across a region that today spans Bangladesh and parts of eastern India.

title: Binary Number System
description: The binary number system is a positional numeral system with base two: each digit is either 0 or 1, and each position represents a power of two. Digital computers use binary representations because electronic circuits can reliably distinguish between two states, although real devices implement those states through physical voltage, charge or other properties. Binary encoding underlies digital arithmetic, memory, instructions and data representation; it is one of several number systems used in mathematics and computing.
short: A base-two positional number system that represents values using only 0 and 1.

title: Algorithms
description: An algorithm is a finite, well-defined procedure that takes specified inputs and produces an output or completes a task. Algorithms are not limited to computers: recipes, arithmetic procedures and navigation instructions can also be described algorithmically. In computing, algorithms are analysed for correctness, resource use and efficiency. The English word derives from the Latinised name of the ninth-century mathematician al-Khwarizmi, whose works helped transmit arithmetic methods.
short: A finite, clearly specified sequence of steps for solving a problem or carrying out a computation.

title: Calculus
description: Calculus is a branch of mathematics concerned with continuous change and accumulation. Differential calculus studies rates of change and slopes using derivatives; integral calculus studies accumulated quantities such as areas and total change. Its foundations developed over many centuries, with important ancient work by Archimedes and later advances by many mathematicians. Isaac Newton and Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz independently developed systematic forms of calculus in the seventeenth century, and their notations shaped later mathematics.
short: A branch of mathematics that studies continuous change through derivatives and accumulation through integrals.

title: Cryptography
description: Cryptography is the study and practice of techniques for protecting information against unauthorized access or manipulation. Modern systems use several complementary tools: encryption supports confidentiality, cryptographic hash functions help detect changes, and digital signatures support authenticity and integrity. Symmetric cryptography uses shared secret keys, while public-key methods use mathematically related key pairs. Secure use depends not only on algorithms but also on sound protocols, key generation, storage and management.
short: The mathematical and computational methods used to protect information and verify digital communication.

title: Linux
description: An open-source operating-system kernel that powers servers, supercomputers, phones and embedded devices.
short: An open-source operating-system kernel that powers servers, supercomputers, phones and embedded devices.

title: Microprocessor
description: A microprocessor is a processor whose central processing functions are implemented on one or a small number of integrated-circuit chips. It combines arithmetic, logic and control operations that were previously built from multiple components. The Intel 4004, introduced commercially in 1971 for a calculator project, is widely recognised as an early single-chip general-purpose microprocessor, but the history includes earlier multi-chip processor sets and parallel development by several teams.
short: A processor implemented on an integrated circuit that performs a computer's central processing functions.

title: Integrated Circuit
description: A complete electronic circuit fabricated on a small semiconductor chip, enabling modern digital electronics.
short: A complete electronic circuit fabricated on a small semiconductor chip, enabling modern digital electronics.

title: Cloud Computing
description: On-demand computing resources delivered over networks, changing how software and infrastructure are operated.
short: On-demand computing resources delivered over networks, changing how software and infrastructure are operated.

title: Blockchain
description: A shared digital ledger structure best known for underpinning Bitcoin and other decentralized systems.
short: A shared digital ledger structure best known for underpinning Bitcoin and other decentralized systems.

title: Machine Learning
description: Methods that allow computers to learn patterns from data and improve at tasks without explicit step-by-step rules.
short: Methods that allow computers to learn patterns from data and improve at tasks without explicit step-by-step rules.

title: Artificial Neural Network
description: A family of computing models inspired by networks of connected neurons, central to modern deep learning.
short: A family of computing models inspired by networks of connected neurons, central to modern deep learning.

title: Theory of Relativity
description: Einstein's theories changed the understanding of space, time, gravity and the relationship between mass and energy.
short: Einstein's theories changed the understanding of space, time, gravity and the relationship between mass and energy.

title: Periodic Table
description: The periodic table arranges chemical elements by increasing atomic number, grouping elements whose properties recur in patterns. Earlier chemists organised elements using observed similarities and atomic masses. Dmitri Mendeleev's 1869 table was influential because it left gaps and predicted properties of elements not yet discovered. Henry Moseley's work on atomic number in the early twentieth century established the basis for the modern ordering.
short: A systematic arrangement of chemical elements that reveals recurring patterns in their properties.

title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging
description: A non-invasive imaging technique that uses magnetic fields and radio waves to create detailed images inside the body.
short: A non-invasive imaging technique that uses magnetic fields and radio waves to create detailed images inside the body.

title: Exoplanets
description: Planets orbiting stars beyond the Sun have revealed that planetary systems are common and remarkably diverse.
short: Planets orbiting stars beyond the Sun have revealed that planetary systems are common and remarkably diverse.

title: Hubble Space Telescope
description: A space-based observatory whose images and measurements transformed astronomy and public views of the universe.
short: A space-based observatory whose images and measurements transformed astronomy and public views of the universe.

title: Black Holes
description: Regions of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape from within the event horizon.
short: Regions of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape from within the event horizon.

title: Mars Exploration Rovers
description: Robotic missions that explored Mars and gathered evidence about the planet's ancient environments and geology.
short: Robotic missions that explored Mars and gathered evidence about the planet's ancient environments and geology.

title: Silk
description: A prized textile whose production and trade connected East Asia with distant markets and helped name the Silk Road.
short: A prized textile whose production and trade connected East Asia with distant markets and helped name the Silk Road.

title: Olympic Games
description: An ancient Greek athletic festival revived in the modern era as an international sporting event.
short: An ancient Greek athletic festival revived in the modern era as an international sporting event.

title: Jazz
description: A musical form rooted in African American communities, known for improvisation, syncopation and evolving styles.
short: A musical form rooted in African American communities, known for improvisation, syncopation and evolving styles.

title: Mona Lisa
description: Leonardo da Vinci's portrait became one of the world's most recognised paintings and an enduring subject of art history.
short: Leonardo da Vinci's portrait became one of the world's most recognised paintings and an enduring subject of art history.

title: William Shakespeare
description: An English playwright and poet whose works continue to shape theatre, literature and the English language.
short: An English playwright and poet whose works continue to shape theatre, literature and the English language.

title: Harry Potter
description: J. K. Rowling's fantasy series became a global publishing phenomenon and influenced modern popular culture.
short: J. K. Rowling's fantasy series became a global publishing phenomenon and influenced modern popular culture.

title: Philosophy
description: The disciplined study of fundamental questions about knowledge, reality, ethics, reason and human existence.
short: The disciplined study of fundamental questions about knowledge, reality, ethics, reason and human existence.

title: Public Education
description: The expansion of organised schooling reshaped literacy, citizenship, social mobility and modern states.
short: The expansion of organised schooling reshaped literacy, citizenship, social mobility and modern states.

title: Human Migration
description: The movement of people across regions and borders has shaped populations, languages, economies and cultures.
short: The movement of people across regions and borders has shaped populations, languages, economies and cultures.

title: Constitutionalism
description: The principle that public power should be organised and limited by a framework of law and institutions.
short: The principle that public power should be organised and limited by a framework of law and institutions.

title: United Nations
description: An international organisation founded after World War II to support cooperation, peace, security and human rights.
short: An international organisation founded after World War II to support cooperation, peace, security and human rights.

title: Civil Rights Movement
description: A broad struggle against racial segregation and discrimination that transformed law and public life in the United States.
short: A broad struggle against racial segregation and discrimination that transformed law and public life in the United States.

title: Plate Tectonics
description: Plate tectonics describes the movement and interaction of large pieces of Earth's lithosphere. Plates move slowly over the deeper, ductile mantle and interact at divergent, convergent and transform boundaries. These processes create and recycle oceanic crust, build mountain belts, and shape the global patterns of earthquakes and volcanoes. The modern theory developed through multiple lines of evidence, including ocean-floor mapping, magnetic patterns, earthquake distributions and seafloor spreading.
short: The theory that Earth's outer rigid shell is divided into moving lithospheric plates.

title: Amazon Rainforest
description: The Amazon rainforest is a vast tropical forest and river basin spanning several South American countries, with most of the forest in Brazil. It stores carbon, influences regional rainfall and supports exceptional biological and cultural diversity. Deforestation, degradation, fire and climate change interact to threaten forest integrity and can alter water and carbon cycles. The Amazon is not a uniform ecosystem: it includes different forest types, wetlands, savannas and seasonally flooded landscapes.
short: A vast and diverse tropical forest and river system in South America with major roles in biodiversity, carbon storage and regional water cycles.

title: Ozone Layer
description: The ozone layer is a region of the stratosphere with relatively high concentrations of ozone that absorbs much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation. Human-made ozone-depleting substances, especially chlorofluorocarbons, release chlorine and bromine compounds that destroy ozone through catalytic chemical reactions. The Montreal Protocol controls these substances, and assessments show a long-term recovery trend, although recovery varies by region and is influenced by atmospheric conditions and other emissions.
short: A stratospheric region containing ozone that absorbs much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.

title: Biodiversity
description: Biodiversity refers to the variety of life at genetic, species and ecosystem levels, together with the ecological relationships that sustain living systems. It supports food production, pollination, soil formation, freshwater quality, climate regulation, medicines and cultural values. The IPBES global assessment synthesised thousands of scientific publications alongside Indigenous and local knowledge, finding widespread declines driven by land- and sea-use change, direct exploitation, climate change, pollution and invasive alien species. Biodiversity is not simply a count of species; it also includes variation within species and the diversity of ecosystems.
short: The variety of life within species, between species and across ecosystems, and the ecological relationships linking them.

title: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
description: A Bengali educator and reformer who campaigned for education, widow remarriage and social change.
short: A Bengali educator and reformer who campaigned for education, widow remarriage and social change.

title: Kazi Nazrul Islam
description: The Bengali poet known as the Rebel Poet, whose writing and music challenged oppression and celebrated human freedom.
short: The Bengali poet known as the Rebel Poet, whose writing and music challenged oppression and celebrated human freedom.

title: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
description: A central leader of the Bengali nationalist movement and the founding president of independent Bangladesh.
short: A central leader of the Bengali nationalist movement and the founding president of independent Bangladesh.

title: Bengal Tiger
description: An iconic big cat of South Asia whose survival is closely tied to the protection of forests and connected habitats.
short: An iconic big cat of South Asia whose survival is closely tied to the protection of forests and connected habitats.

title: Muslin of Bengal
description: Fine cotton muslin produced in Bengal became renowned in international trade for its lightness and craftsmanship.
short: Fine cotton muslin produced in Bengal became renowned in international trade for its lightness and craftsmanship.

title: Bangla Language
description: An Indo-Aryan language with a rich literary history and a central place in the cultural identity of Bangladesh and West Bengal.
short: An Indo-Aryan language with a rich literary history and a central place in the cultural identity of Bangladesh and West Bengal.

title: Economics
description: The study of how people, businesses and societies make choices about resources, production and exchange.
short: The study of how people, businesses and societies make choices about resources, production and exchange.

title: Money
description: A widely accepted medium of exchange that makes trade, pricing and saving possible across complex societies.
short: A widely accepted medium of exchange that makes trade, pricing and saving possible across complex societies.

title: Inflation
description: A sustained rise in the general price level that reduces the purchasing power of money over time.
short: A sustained rise in the general price level that reduces the purchasing power of money over time.

title: Stock Market
description: A marketplace where shares in companies are issued and traded, helping businesses raise capital and investors share in ownership.
short: A marketplace where shares in companies are issued and traded, helping businesses raise capital and investors share in ownership.

title: Civil Engineering
description: Civil engineering applies scientific and engineering principles to the planning, design, construction, operation and maintenance of infrastructure. Its fields include structural, geotechnical, transportation, water-resources, environmental and construction engineering. Civil engineers must account for loads, materials, soil, water, hazards, accessibility, cost, lifecycle maintenance and environmental impacts. The discipline supports public systems such as buildings, roads, bridges, ports, water supply and wastewater treatment.
short: The engineering discipline concerned with infrastructure and the built environment.

title: Robotics
description: The design, construction and use of robots, combining mechanics, electronics, sensing and computation.
short: The design, construction and use of robots, combining mechanics, electronics, sensing and computation.

title: Bridge
description: A bridge is a structure that carries a route or utility across an obstacle such as a river, valley, road or railway. Common structural forms include beam, arch, truss, cantilever, suspension and cable-stayed bridges. Design depends on span, loads, foundations, materials, wind, seismic conditions, durability, construction method and maintenance. Bridges are engineered for a specific site and service life rather than selected from one universal design.
short: A structure that spans a physical obstacle to carry people, vehicles, railways or utilities.

title: Irrigation
description: Irrigation is the controlled application of water to land or crops to support plant growth when rainfall is insufficient or poorly timed. Systems include surface or gravity-fed methods, sprinklers and localized drip irrigation, each with different costs, energy needs, water efficiencies and suitability. Irrigation can increase agricultural productivity, but poor management can contribute to waterlogging, salinity, groundwater depletion and competition for water.
short: The planned supply of water to agricultural land or plants to support growth.

title: Domestication
description: The gradual adaptation of plants and animals to human cultivation and care, transforming food systems and settlement.
short: The gradual adaptation of plants and animals to human cultivation and care, transforming food systems and settlement.

title: Fermentation
description: A microbial process used for millennia to make and preserve foods and drinks, from bread and yoghurt to pickles.
short: A microbial process used for millennia to make and preserve foods and drinks, from bread and yoghurt to pickles.

title: Crop Rotation
description: The practice of growing different crops in sequence to maintain soil fertility and manage pests and diseases.
short: The practice of growing different crops in sequence to maintain soil fertility and manage pests and diseases.

title: Telegraph
description: A system that transmitted messages over long distances using coded electrical signals, transforming news and business in the nineteenth century.
short: A system that transmitted messages over long distances using coded electrical signals, transforming news and business in the nineteenth century.

title: Television
description: A system for transmitting moving images and sound, becoming a defining medium of news, entertainment and shared culture.
short: A system for transmitting moving images and sound, becoming a defining medium of news, entertainment and shared culture.

title: Broadcasting
description: The distribution of audio or video content to audiences through radio, television and digital networks.
short: The distribution of audio or video content to audiences through radio, television and digital networks.

title: Mobile Communication
description: Wireless communication between devices over cellular and other radio networks, making information accessible while moving.
short: Wireless communication between devices over cellular and other radio networks, making information accessible while moving.

title: Archaeology
description: The study of past human life through material remains, from buildings and tools to landscapes and buried objects.
short: The study of past human life through material remains, from buildings and tools to landscapes and buried objects.

title: Rosetta Stone
description: An inscribed stone whose parallel texts helped scholars decipher Egyptian hieroglyphs in the nineteenth century.
short: An inscribed stone whose parallel texts helped scholars decipher Egyptian hieroglyphs in the nineteenth century.

title: Pompeii
description: A Roman city preserved beneath volcanic material after the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE, offering an unusually detailed view of ancient life.
short: A Roman city preserved beneath volcanic material after the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE, offering an unusually detailed view of ancient life.

title: Terracotta Army
description: Thousands of life-size clay figures buried with China's first emperor, revealing the scale and organisation of Qin power.
short: Thousands of life-size clay figures buried with China's first emperor, revealing the scale and organisation of Qin power.

title: University
description: An institution for advanced teaching, research and the preservation and creation of knowledge.
short: An institution for advanced teaching, research and the preservation and creation of knowledge.

title: Literacy
description: The ability to read and write, a foundation for education, participation in public life and access to information.
short: The ability to read and write, a foundation for education, participation in public life and access to information.

title: Library
description: An organised collection of books and information that preserves knowledge and makes it available to communities.
short: An organised collection of books and information that preserves knowledge and makes it available to communities.

title: Massive Open Online Course
description: An online course designed for large-scale participation, expanding access to learning beyond traditional classrooms.
short: An online course designed for large-scale participation, expanding access to learning beyond traditional classrooms.

title: Psychology
year: Late 19th century as a formal scientific discipline
short: The scientific study of mind, behaviour and experience.
description: Psychology is the scientific study of mind, behaviour and experience. It investigates how people think, feel, learn and act, drawing on methods from experiments, observation, neuroscience and social research. Modern experimental psychology emerged as a distinct academic discipline in the nineteenth century.

title: Psychoanalysis
short: A tradition of exploring unconscious processes, inner conflict and the influence of early experience.
description: A tradition of exploring unconscious processes, inner conflict and the influence of early experience.

title: Cognitive Psychology
short: The study of how people perceive, remember, reason, learn and use language.
description: The study of how people perceive, remember, reason, learn and use language.

title: Behaviorism
short: An approach that studies observable behaviour and how it is shaped by learning and the environment.
description: An approach that studies observable behaviour and how it is shaped by learning and the environment.

title: Social Psychology
short: The study of how people think, feel and act in social situations and groups.
description: The study of how people think, feel and act in social situations and groups.

title: Architecture
short: The art and practice of shaping buildings and places for human use, meaning and experience.
description: The art and practice of shaping buildings and places for human use, meaning and experience.

title: Bauhaus
short: A modernist school that brought art, craft and industrial design into a shared approach to everyday objects and buildings.
description: A modernist school that brought art, craft and industrial design into a shared approach to everyday objects and buildings.

title: Gothic Architecture
short: A medieval style recognised for pointed arches, ribbed vaults and soaring spaces filled with light.
description: A medieval style recognised for pointed arches, ribbed vaults and soaring spaces filled with light.

title: Modern Architecture
short: A movement that favoured new materials, functional planning and forms shaped by modern life.
description: A movement that favoured new materials, functional planning and forms shaped by modern life.

title: Sustainable Architecture
short: Designing buildings to reduce environmental impact through energy efficiency, materials and climate-aware planning.
description: Designing buildings to reduce environmental impact through energy efficiency, materials and climate-aware planning.

title: Energy
year: A fundamental concept studied since antiquity
short: The capacity to do work, transformed between forms that power natural processes and human technology.
description: The capacity to do work, transformed between forms that power natural processes and human technology.

title: Solar Energy
year: Ancient use; modern photovoltaic technology from the 19th century
short: Using sunlight to produce heat or electricity, increasingly important in the transition to low-carbon energy.
description: Using sunlight to produce heat or electricity, increasingly important in the transition to low-carbon energy.

title: Wind Power
year: Ancient use; modern wind turbines from the 19th century
short: Generating electricity by converting the motion of air into mechanical and electrical power.
description: Generating electricity by converting the motion of air into mechanical and electrical power.

title: Nuclear Power
short: Generating electricity from heat released by controlled nuclear fission in a reactor.
description: Generating electricity from heat released by controlled nuclear fission in a reactor.

title: Battery
short: An electrochemical device that stores energy chemically and delivers it as electrical power.
description: A battery is an electrochemical device that stores energy in chemical form and converts it into electrical energy when connected to a circuit. Cells typically contain two electrodes and an electrolyte; during discharge, electrochemical reactions drive electrons through the external circuit while ions move inside the cell. Rechargeable batteries use reactions that can be driven in reverse, although repeated cycling causes degradation. Different chemistries trade off energy density, power, cost, safety, lifespan and material availability.

title: Linguistics
year: 19th century as a modern academic discipline
short: The scientific study of language, including its sounds, structures, meanings and social use.
description: The scientific study of language, including its sounds, structures, meanings and social use.

title: Phonetics
year: Ancient study; modern experimental science from the 19th century
short: The study of speech sounds, how they are produced, transmitted and heard.
description: The study of speech sounds, how they are produced, transmitted and heard.

title: Writing Systems
short: The different ways languages are represented visually, from alphabets to syllabaries and logographic systems.
description: The different ways languages are represented visually, from alphabets to syllabaries and logographic systems.

title: Sign Languages
year: Long history; documented sign languages vary by community
short: Full natural languages that use visual and manual forms rather than sound, with their own grammar and communities.
description: Full natural languages that use visual and manual forms rather than sound, with their own grammar and communities.

title: Translation
short: The practice of carrying meaning between languages, connecting literature, science, diplomacy and everyday life.
description: The practice of carrying meaning between languages, connecting literature, science, diplomacy and everyday life.

title: Cinema
short: The art and technology of moving images and screen storytelling.
description: Cinema is the art, industry and technology of moving images. It combines photography, performance, editing, sound and storytelling, developing into a global medium for entertainment, documentary, education and cultural expression.

title: Animation
short: Creating the illusion of movement through sequences of images, drawings, models or digital frames.
description: Creating the illusion of movement through sequences of images, drawings, models or digital frames.

title: Documentary Film
short: Non-fiction filmmaking that records, interprets or investigates real people, events and ideas.
description: Non-fiction filmmaking that records, interprets or investigates real people, events and ideas.

title: Film Editing
short: The craft of selecting and arranging shots to shape a film's rhythm, meaning and emotional impact.
description: The craft of selecting and arranging shots to shape a film's rhythm, meaning and emotional impact.

title: Sound Recording
short: The capture and reproduction of sound, transforming music, broadcasting, cinema and personal communication.
description: The capture and reproduction of sound, transforming music, broadcasting, cinema and personal communication.

title: Ethics
year: Ancient roots; developed across philosophical traditions
short: The study of how people ought to live, act and treat one another.
description: Ethics examines questions about right and wrong, virtue, duties, justice and the good life. Philosophical traditions approach these questions through different methods, including consequences, principles, character, relationships and lived experience.

title: Metaphysics
short: Questions about what exists and the fundamental nature of reality.
description: Metaphysics investigates the most general features of reality: what exists, what makes things the same or different, how cause and time work, and how mind relates to matter. Its questions range from everyday objects to possibility, identity and the nature of being.

title: Epistemology
short: The study of knowledge, belief, evidence and justification.
description: Epistemology asks what knowledge is, how beliefs are justified, what counts as evidence and where the limits of human understanding lie. It connects philosophy with science, perception, memory, testimony and reasoning.

title: Human Rights
short: Basic rights and freedoms belonging to every person.
description: Human rights are claims and protections grounded in the dignity and equal worth of people. They are expressed through moral arguments, national constitutions and international instruments, including treaties developed through the United Nations system.

title: Rule of Law
year: Long historical development; modern international framework
short: The principle that public power is constrained by known and fairly applied laws.
description: The rule of law means that individuals, institutions and governments are accountable under publicly known rules. It depends on fair procedures, independent institutions, access to justice and protections against arbitrary uses of power.

title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
short: A landmark United Nations declaration setting out a common standard of human rights.
description: Adopted by the UN General Assembly on 10 December 1948, the Universal Declaration of Human Rights sets out 30 articles on civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights. It is a declaration rather than a treaty, but it became a foundation for later international human-rights instruments.

title: Music
short: Organised sound shaped by rhythm, melody, harmony, timbre and culture.
description: Music is a human art and social practice found in every known society. It can accompany ritual, storytelling, work, celebration, protest and entertainment, while musical systems and meanings vary widely across cultures and historical periods.

title: Musical Instruments
short: Tools that produce sound through vibration, from drums to digital synthesizers.
description: Musical instruments create sound through vibrating strings, air columns, membranes, solid materials or electronic signals. Their design reflects local materials, musical traditions, craftsmanship and changing technologies.

title: Human Origins
year: Human evolutionary history spans millions of years
short: The study of how human beings evolved and became diverse communities.
description: Research into human origins draws on fossils, genetics, archaeology, comparative anatomy and studies of ancient environments. The evidence describes a branching evolutionary history rather than a simple straight line from one species to another.

title: Cultural Anthropology
year: Developed as a modern academic field in the 19th–20th centuries
short: The study of human cultures, social practices, meanings and everyday life.
description: Cultural anthropology studies how people organise social life and make meaning through language, kinship, belief, exchange, art and institutions. Ethnographic research often involves long-term observation and learning from the perspectives of the communities being studied.

title: Ocean Currents
short: Large-scale movements of seawater driven by wind, density differences and other forces.
description: Ocean currents move water through surface and deep-ocean pathways. Driven by winds, differences in temperature and salinity, tides and Earth's rotation, they redistribute heat and nutrients and influence climate, marine ecosystems and fisheries.

title: Coral Reef Ecosystems
short: Highly diverse marine ecosystems built by reef-forming corals and associated organisms.
description: Coral reefs are marine ecosystems built largely by colonies of coral animals that produce calcium-carbonate structures. Their complex habitats support high biodiversity, fisheries, tourism and coastal protection. Reefs are sensitive to marine heatwaves, which can cause coral bleaching, as well as ocean acidification, pollution, sedimentation and destructive fishing. Coral bleaching is a stress response and does not always mean a coral has died, but prolonged or repeated stress can cause severe reef decline.

title: The Deep Sea
year: A major frontier of modern ocean exploration
short: The vast, dark ocean environment beyond the reach of sunlight.
description: The deep sea includes immense areas of the ocean where sunlight is absent or extremely limited. It contains specialised ecosystems, hydrothermal vents, deep-sea corals and species adapted to cold, darkness and high pressure, many of which remain poorly studied.

title: Gravitational Waves
short: Ripples in spacetime produced by accelerating masses.
description: Gravitational waves are disturbances in spacetime generated by accelerating masses. The first direct detection in 2015 came from the merger of two black holes, opening a new way to study extreme cosmic events alongside traditional astronomy.

title: Prime Numbers
short: The indivisible building blocks of whole-number arithmetic, with deep links to patterns and cryptography.
description: A prime number is an integer greater than 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and itself. Every integer greater than 1 can be expressed uniquely as a product of primes, making primes the basic building blocks of arithmetic. Euclid proved that there are infinitely many primes, yet their detailed distribution remains a rich area of research. Prime numbers also underpin important cryptographic systems, where the difficulty of certain number-theoretic problems helps protect digital communication.

title: Modular Arithmetic
short: Arithmetic in which integers are considered equivalent when they leave the same remainder after division by a fixed positive integer.
description: Modular arithmetic studies congruences such as a ≡ b (mod n), meaning that a and b differ by a multiple of n. It turns the integers into repeating remainder systems and supports calculations with clocks, cyclic patterns and divisibility. Important results include the Euclidean algorithm, Fermat's little theorem and the Chinese remainder theorem. Modular arithmetic is a foundation of elementary number theory and is used in cryptographic algorithms and error-detecting systems.

title: Euclidean Geometry
short: Euclidean Geometry explores a key idea, method or development within geometry.
description: Euclidean Geometry explores a key idea, method or development within geometry. Its history, evidence and applications connect this field to wider scientific, historical and cultural questions.

title: Non-Euclidean Geometry
short: Non-Euclidean Geometry explores a key idea, method or development within geometry.
description: Non-Euclidean Geometry explores a key idea, method or development within geometry. Its history, evidence and applications connect this field to wider scientific, historical and cultural questions.

title: Probability
short: A mathematical framework for describing uncertainty and the likelihood of events.
description: Probability assigns numerical measures to events in a model of uncertainty. It provides rules for combining events and reasoning about conditional outcomes, independence and long-run frequencies. Probability does not guarantee the result of an individual random event; instead, it supports coherent predictions across repeated trials and uncertain systems. It underlies statistics, scientific inference, risk analysis, communications, finance, epidemiology and many areas of computer science.
